children: Salesforce is spending billions on another artificial-intelligence acquisition. Wall Street is debating whether the price is worth it.

On Tuesday, Salesforce said it is acquire marketing software company Braze in an all-cash deal valued at nearly $5.7 billion. Salesforce will pay $47.50 a share, representing a roughly 58% premium to the Braze's closing price of $30.04 on Monday.

The companies said the transaction is expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal 2028, pending shareholder and regulatory approvals. Salesforce said it doesn't anticipate any changes to its fiscal 2027 financial guidance as a result of the deal.

Shares of Braze surged 51% to $45.31, putting the stock on pace for its largest daily percentage increase on record, according to Dow Jones Market Data. The rally brought shares closer to Salesforce's offer price, suggesting investors expect the deal to go through. Salesforce shares fell 1%. Braze rival Klaviyo jumped 8.9%.

Salesforce said the acquisition would bolster its marketing software offerings with Braze's AI-powered technology, which helps businesses personalize customer interactions across websites, mobile apps, email, and text messages.
The deal fits into Salesforce's broader strategy of adding AI capabilities across its software business.

Salesforce agreed to acquire Informatica for about $8 billion in May 2025, aiming to improve the data infrastructure supporting its AI products. In June, it announced a $3.6 billion deal for AI customer-service provider Fin.

Those investments have already helped lift Salesforce's revenue growth. The company said in its fiscal second-quarter earnings report that revenue was expected to grow 11% to 12% in fiscal 2027, with its Informatica acquisition accounting for slightly more than three percentage points.

In its quarterly report, Salesforce also raised its fiscal-year revenue forecast by $200 million, partly reflecting expected contributions from its pending acquisitions of Contentful, a content-management software company, and Fin.
The Braze acquisition is what Evercore ISI analysts zeroed in on. They question the cost and timing, noting Salesforce's offer represents an 80% premium to Braze's 30-day moving average.
The premium, they wrote, "seems a bit odd unless it was competitive."

And, the analysts said, the pace of Salesforce's acquisitions is "likely to raise eyebrows" among investors looking for reasonably priced starks with strong growth prospects. They suggested rival ServiceNow could benefit as investors shift away from Salesforce.
More acquisitions could make it harder for investors to assess growth in Salesforce's underlying business, they added.

BTIG analysts were more optimistic, arguing the acquisition makes strategic sense given the fragmented market for marketing software. They expect the transaction to close and estimate Salesforce will pay about 5.3 times Braze's projected fiscal 2028 revenue of $1.07 billion.
